title: Restriction is constant when all relevant coordinates are fixed
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $J,P\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Fix an assignment $z$ on $P$. If $f$ depends only on coordinates in $J$ and $J\subseteq P$, then the restriction of $f$ obtained by fixing $P$ according to $z$ is constant on all assignments to the remaining coordinates, with value given by evaluating $f$ at the cube point formed from $z$ on $P$ and the all-positive assignment outside $P$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function on the n-dimensional sign cube
Finite coordinate sets J and P
